questions.stem: What is CaaS (Container as a Service) about?
options: Deploying code in a container and deploying that container in the Cloud
Subscribing to a pre-built business solution
Pulling data on demand through APIs
Renting office space for IT teams
questions.explanation: As the name says, CaaS is about deploying code in a container and deploying that container in the Cloud.

questions.stem: How is CaaS positioned relative to IaaS in the cloud rental hierarchy?
questions.explanation: CaaS is described as one level lower than IaaS for renting resources on the Cloud, at a smaller scale.

questions.stem: What does CaaS save the customer from having to do?
options: Managing hardware on their own in the Cloud
questions.explanation: With CaaS the customer deploys containers and the underlying hardware is managed by the Cloud provider, unlike IaaS.

questions.stem: What are the stated motivations for renting containers rather than whole infrastructure?
options: Saving cost and better management of resources
questions.explanation: Renting containers at a small scale saves cost and gives better management of resources.

questions.stem: Which methodology is CaaS described as being very helpful for?
questions.explanation: In Agile, multiple teams work in silos on different modules, and CaaS lets each develop and deploy their code set at any time using CI/CD pipelines.

questions.stem: In Agile projects, why is CaaS particularly useful for multiple teams?
options: Because it forces all teams to deploy together once a quarter
Because it removes the need for sprints
Because it merges all modules into one container
Because different teams can develop and deploy their code sets at any time
questions.explanation: CaaS lets different teams, working in silos on different modules, develop and deploy their own code sets at any time.

questions.stem: What does IaaS rent from Cloud providers, in contrast to CaaS?
questions.explanation: With IaaS only hardware is rented; CaaS is the next stage where containers are rented instead.

questions.stem: Which statement about CaaS availability is made?
options: Only one Cloud provider offers it
It is not yet offered by any Cloud provider
Most of the Cloud providers are offering CaaS
questions.explanation: The topic states that most of the Cloud providers are offering CaaS.

questions.stem: Under CaaS, who manages the hardware underneath the deployed containers?
questions.explanation: Customers deploy their containers and underneath them the hardware is managed by the Cloud providers.

questions.stem: CaaS is described as the next stage of which paradigm change?
options: Moving from Cloud back to On-Premises
Moving from renting hardware (IaaS) to renting containers at a smaller scale
questions.explanation: After On-Premises versus Cloud and IaaS, the next stage of the paradigm change is renting containers at a small scale.
